research_question: Does a pre-specified pathway-aware model yield better calibrated and more transportable prediction of selected population-level physical phenotypes than an age, cohort, site, and measurement-process baseline?

hypotheses.statement: At least one pathway-aware model will improve locked temporal and external-site proper scoring and calibration over baseline without failing robustness gates.
hypotheses.falsified_if: No locked improvement is observed or calibration, robustness, or governance gates fail.

hypotheses.statement: For third-molar agenesis, separating congenital status from extraction, impaction, eruption, and treatment will change descriptive interpretation relative to an undifferentiated dental record.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Endpoint harmonisation shows no material misclassification or cannot be performed.

outcomes.name: Congenital third-molar agenesis
outcomes.measurement_rule: Age-adequate developmental source record with explicit exclusion or separate coding of extraction, impaction, eruption, and treatment.

outcomes.name: Pre-specified craniofacial scalar measures
outcomes.measurement_rule: Approved, de-identified scalar measurements only; raw facial images are excluded from release.

outcomes.name: Standardised anthropometric measure
outcomes.measurement_rule: Use only harmonised or explicitly modelled instrument protocols.

robustness: negative-control outcome or exposure where defensible

forecast_claim_allowed_only_if: Temporal and external-site performance improves under the registered criterion.
Calibration and reliability pass all adequately powered prespecified strata.
Results survive measurement, composition, and genetic-block sensitivity analyses.
Consent, privacy, domain-specialist, statistical, and communications reviews approve.
decision_rule.otherwise: Report a descriptive or null result; do not assert a future human phenotype trajectory.

stop_conditions: No lawful data-use basis or inadequate consent
Cannot separate congenital absence from treatment history
Unharmonized measurements dominate site or cohort effects
Insufficient support for calibrated subgroup assessment
Result communication cannot avoid deterministic group claims
